world.topic:
Analyse the DojoWorld worlds given you to read and propose what their next round should change.

The worlds: dw_3a18fd6e1d02 (N1, a fresh world), dw_1475d43aee7b (N2, continuing N1) and dw_a42fcf98e9a5 (T, continuing N2, a round that only evaluates). They train the paper-writing worker of a research world and judge it on held-out tasks; the research worlds their positions made are given to read too. The earlier rounds of the same line, dw_59f01b2fe95e, dw_ae1c3437dfc5, dw_d2d2045ec28f and dw_ee16b8f7253e, are given as history. All seven have ended. The user drove these worlds and changed their configuration on the way (`config history` shows each change); the user's own notes on them are not given.

1. Diagnose every problem these worlds show: its kind, its place and the records that show it.
2. Problems a definition, a domain's implementation or the kernel must change for: one pull request to a-green-hand-jack/HuTian-KaiTian, base dev; merging it is the maintainer's decision. Change nothing that only a worker did, and keep each change small. If there is none, say why.
3. Problems only in workers' behavior: a draft objective for DojoWorld's next round, in your repository. The maintainer decides whether to run it.
4. Try the pull request on trial-machine: install it there, build its images, run the repository's regression checks there, and run a fresh world of each domain it changes to its release with a tiny task and Claude Code claude-sonnet-5-5 at low effort ($CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN), at most 40 executions and 3000 model seconds over the trial world and every world it makes. The pull request says what changed, which findings it answers and how the trial ended (the trial world's id and its release).
